blocks.text: Scheduling a professional sump pump installation in Alamo Heights, TX, protects your home from water damage. While it may tempt you to take on this task yourself to save money, working with a professional is ideal. We help you determine what kind of sump pump you need, find the best location for it, and install it according to local codes. If you experience any problems with your sump pump at any point, Rosenberg Plumbing & Air offers prompt sump pump repair services to get you back on track before extensive damage occurs.

When choosing a sump pump for your home, consider several factors. Key aspects include horsepower and gallons-per-minute ratings. A sump pump with a horsepower of 1/3 works well for residences with a low water table. If you live in a very damp area, you can upgrade to ¾ to 1 horsepower. Dense soil containing a lot of clay requires a pump with a gallons-per-minute rating of approximately 8 GPM per 1,000 square feet. A rating of 14 GPM per 1,000 square feet works for sandy soil. The decibel rating of your sump pump matters as well. You want it to operate quietly, especially if it is located near bedrooms or living rooms.

We pay close attention to the location of your pump. Our team will install this equipment in your basement, at the lowest possible point. Water will collect in this pit and then be pumped away from your home through a drain line. Over time, frequent use of your sump pump can cause wear and tear. We can perform a routine inspection to determine if certain parts, such as seals, pumps, motors, and bearings, require replacement or repair. We also inspect your GFCI outlet to ensure the safe operation of your pump.

If the power goes out in your home, it can prevent your pump from functioning, which leads to water backing up in your basement and causing damage. Consider installing a battery backup. When the power goes out, the battery engages and allows your pump to continue working. Another option is to have us install a water-powered sump pump as your backup. A water-powered sump pump uses municipal water pressure to remove basement water, providing reliable backup during power outages or primary pump failures and preventing flooding damage.
